mstts:express-as.prosody: Chapter 8: Letting Go Without Forgetting. You know, there comes a time when holding on just starts to feel heavy. Maybe it’s a box of old mixtapes, a stack of photos, or those little mementos you’ve tucked away in the back of a drawer. They’re all reminders of what used to be—pieces of a life that’s changed. But sometimes, those reminders can make it tough to step forward. For someone who’s lost a partner, letting go can feel almost wrong. As if moving forward means you’re leaving the past behind, or even erasing it completely. But here’s the thing—memory and hope aren’t enemies. They can sit side by side. Picture this: one afternoon, he’s cleaning out a closet and stumbles across a box of old tapes he hasn’t seen in years. Some of the labels are written in a familiar hand, others are blank—little mysteries waiting to be heard. So, he sits right down on the floor, pops in a tape, and lets the music fill the room. Some songs make him laugh, some bring tears. But through it all, there’s this deep sense of gratitude—grateful for the life he shared, and for the soundtrack that made it richer. Letting go, though, isn’t about forgetting. The past is still there, woven into every note and lyric. But there’s something else, too—a sense that maybe, just maybe, the future doesn’t have to be shaped only by what’s been lost. Most folks don’t realize just how much strength it takes to let go, to open up space for something new. It’s not about erasing old songs—it’s about adding new ones to the playlist. As time goes by, he starts to build new rituals. He makes tapes for friends, for family, even for himself. Each time he picks out a song or tells a little story through the music, it’s a way to honor where he’s been while saying yes to where he is now. There’s a quiet kind of happiness in finding new music—songs that feel right for this chapter in his life. Letting go isn’t just one moment, is it? It’s a process—a bunch of small choices, day after day. Some days, the memories are vivid and close. Other days, the future feels wide open, full of possibility. And often, you don’t even notice how much you’ve grown until you look back and realize just how far you’ve come.
